announcements.title: Headteacher's Message: Welcome to this week’s school newsletter!
announcements.content:
Welcome to this week’s school
newsletter!

It has been another

busy and
engaging week at school,

with lots
happening across our classrooms and
wider school community. We kindly
ask all parents and carers to

take a
little time to read through this week’s
newsletter carefully

, as it contains
several important updates and
reminders. This week, you’ll find
news and information not only from
the

School Office

, but also from our

Catering Team and PTFA

, so please
do have a good peruse to make sure
you don’t miss anything!

With

School Election Day taking
place next Friday,

we know some of
our candidates have been busy
preparing! If your child is standing
for election and has a

PowerPoint
presentation they would like to share,

please send this to

office@wpa.education

by

Monday
morning.

We’re really looking forward to
hearing from our candidates and
wish everyone taking part

the very
best of luck!

🌟

announcements.title: School Reminders: Inhalers, Absences & School Dinners
announcements.content:
Important News

and Reminders

Uniform Donations

We are very grateful for all the
uniform donations we receive.
However,

we kindly ask that parents
and carers do not bring any more
uniform donations into school at this
time,

as we currently have plenty of
stock. The only items we are still able
to accept are

clean, good-condition
uniform with the school logo

,
specifically:

Jumpers and cardigans

PE tops

Hoodies

Thank you for your understanding
and continued support.

Late Arrivals to School - Update

To help us maintain confidentiality
and ensure accurate records, we are
introducing a new procedure for
children arriving late to school. From
now on, parents and carers who bring
their child to school after the
registration period will be asked to
complete a

Lateness Form

at the
school office, providing the reason for
the late arrival.

This change has been introduced for
two important reasons:

Confidentiality

– At busy times,
there may be other parents, visitors
or professionals waiting in the
reception area. Completing a form
allows families to share
information privately rather than
discussing personal circumstances
openly.

Safeguarding and Attendance
Monitoring

– Keeping accurate
records of reasons for lateness
helps us monitor attendance
patterns, identify any concerns,
and provide support where
persistent lateness may be affecting
a child's education.

We appreciate your support and
cooperation in helping us ensure that
all children arrive at school on time
and that our attendance records
remain accurate and up to date.

Clubs Reminder

We are pleased to let families know
that all after-school clubs will begin
on

Monday 21st September

. Please
note that there will be

no clubs on
Wednesday 8th October or Thursday
9th October

due to

Individual School
Photographs

taking place on those
days.

Just to confirm that on days when
children attend an after-school sports
club, they are very welcome to come
to school wearing their approved PE
kit. To help keep children warm and
comfortable during the school day, a
school jumper or cardigan (which
forms part of the school uniform) may
be worn over their PE kit. Thank you,
as always, for your continued
support. If you have any questions,
please feel free to contact the school
office.

🍽️ Catering Team Update – The
Lucky Plate! 🍽️

Every Monday, children enjoying a
cooked school meal have the chance to
discover a

Lucky Plate!

There is

one Lucky Plate winner in
Early Years, one in KS1, and one in
KS2

each week. Winners will find a

Lucky Plate sticker underneath their
dinner plate

during lunchtime. Each
lucky winner will receive a

small
prize

, and their name will also be
entered into our

end-of-year prize
draw,

where they will have the
chance to win an even bigger prize in

July!

We hope this adds a little extra
excitement to Monday lunchtimes.
Good luck everyone, and keep an eye
out for those Lucky Plate stickers!

Diwali Dance Workshop – EYFS &
KS1

On Friday 6th November, our EYFS
and KS1 children will take part in an
exciting Diwali Dance Workshop as
part of their learning about festivals
and celebrations. Led by a
professional dance instructor, the
workshop will bring the story of the
Ramayana to life through movement,
music, and dance, giving children a
fun and engaging insight into the
Hindu Festival of Lights.

Photographs and videos from the day
will be shared with families via Class
Dojo so you can enjoy seeing your
child take part in this special
experience. Thank you to all families
for your support in helping us provide
enriching learning opportunities for
our children. ✨

Inhalers in School

If your child requires an inhaler
whilst at school, please ensure that it
is brought to the school office as soon
as possible. To help us keep our
records accurate and ensure we can
safely administer medication when
needed, parents and carers are also
asked to complete an updated
Medication Administration Form.
Having an in-date inhaler and
current medical information available
is essential for keeping all children
safe and well during the school day.

If you have any questions, please
contact the school office who will be
happy to help.

Reporting Absences and Illness

A gentle reminder to all parents and
carers that if your child is absent
from school due to illness or any
other reason, please notify the

school
office directly

rather than (or as well
as) informing your child's class
teacher.

This helps us to ensure that all
absences are recorded accurately and
that we know your child is safe.
Messages sent to class teachers may
not always be seen or relayed
promptly, particularly during
teaching time.

You can contact the school office by
telephone, email, or using the school's
usual absence reporting system.
Thank you for your cooperation in
helping us maintain accurate
attendance records and safeguard our
pupils.

School Dinners - Reminder

We’ve have noticed an increase in
school dinners being booked via the
app, but children then arriving with a
packed lunch instead.

We kindly ask that if your plans
change and your child no longer
requires a school meal, you

cancel the
booking in advance or let the office
know

. Our kitchen team prepares
meals ahead of the day based on the
numbers provided, so any unclaimed
dinners unfortunately result in
unnecessary food waste.

We are currently monitoring this over
the first few weeks back with a view
to begin charging for missed meals
where bookings have not been
cancelled.

At the same time, we would like to
remind families of the importance of

pre-booking school dinners

to ensure
we can plan effectively and provide
for all pupils. Thank you for your
continued support.

Mexican Menu Day

We’re excited to be holding a

Mexican
Menu Day on Wednesday 23rd
September!

Our catering team have put together
a tasty themed menu for the children.

Please see below for the full menu

and
discover what’s being served!

announcements.title: Attendance Update: Termly Pizza Parties (TAPP) & Appointment Guidelines
announcements.content:
Attendance Update for
September

As we begin the new academic year,
we are introducing a few updates to
our attendance procedures to support
pupils' success and celebrate excellent
attendance.

Medical appointments

will continue
to be authorised only when
appointment confirmation is provided
to the school office.

Optician
appointments

will no longer be
authorised from September, as these
can usually be arranged outside
school hours.

We are also delighted to launch our

Termly Attendance Pizza Parties
(TAPP).

Pupils achieving

98%
attendance or above

each term will be
invited to a special pizza party during
the final week of term and will
receive a raffle ticket for the chance
to win a

£50 Amazon voucher.

At Warboys Primary Academy, we
know that good attendance plays a
vital role in children's academic
achievement, social development and
wellbeing. Thank you for your
continued support in helping your
child attend school regularly and
arrive on time, giving them the very
best opportunity to thrive.

Term-time leave

We appreciate that unexpected events
can happen, and we’re always here to
support families where possible.

However, Cambridgeshire County
Council and the Department for
Education require schools to
authorise leave

only in exceptional
circumstances

—meaning rare,
unavoidable events.

Routine family holidays or planned
trips unfortunately do not meet this
threshold. You can find further
information here:

Non-attendance at school and the
law | Cambridgeshire County
Council

Thank you for your understanding
and cooperation.

announcements.title: Young Carers: Support & Parent Concern Form
announcements.content:
At our school, we are proud to
support our Young Carers and
recognise the important role they
play within their families. We work
closely with Centre 33 to provide
external support, while internally we
offer fortnightly Young Carers
sessions where children can come
together to chat, share experiences,
take part in activities, and relax in a
supportive environment. Led by Miss
Coles and Mrs Flisher, with support
from Mr Bostock, these sessions help
ensure our Young Carers feel valued,
understood, and supported. We are
also committed to raising awareness
across the school community and
celebrating the dedication, resilience,
and compassion shown by our Young
Carers every day.

Please follow the link below to flag
any child that you may deem to be a
Young Carer. A Young Carer is a
child young person who helps to look
after a family member who may have
an illness, disability, mental health
difficulty, or who may need extra
support for another reason. This care
can include practical tasks, emotional
support, or helping siblings, and it
may take place before or after the
school day. We recognise that these
responsibilities can sometimes impact
a child’s wellbeing, learning, and
emotional needs. All conversations
and responses will be treated
sensitively and in confidence.

announcements.title: P.T.F.A: Pre-Loved School Uniform Sales
announcements.content:
A Word from the

P.T.F.A

💛 Could you help keep our PTFA
going?

Our PTFA is a wonderful part of the
Warboys Primary Academy
community, helping to bring exciting
events and opportunities to our
children while raising much-needed
funds for the school.However,

we
urgently need more parents and carers
to get involved.

Following several of our valued
committee members stepping down
as their children finished at the
school last year, we are now facing a
very real challenge.

We are losing our
Treasurer, along with other
experienced members, and without
enough people willing to step forward,
we may have no choice but to fold the
PTFA.

We really don't want that to happen.
You might think you need lots of free
time or previous experience to join
the PTFA,

you don't!

We need people
who can help in whatever way they
can. That could mean helping at an
event, coming along with ideas,
taking on a committee role, helping
with fundraising, or simply lending a
hand occasionally.

Every person who gets involved
makes the workload lighter for
everyone else — and helps us
continue providing those extra
experiences and opportunities
for our children.

📅 PTFA AGM Tuesday 13th
October at 6pm:

Warboys Primary
Academy

Please come along, even if you're
unsure how you could help. Come and
meet the current PTFA, find out what
we do and see how you might be able
to get involved.

We genuinely need
your support. Without new volunteers,
the PTFA may not be able to continue.

Let's make sure we can keep doing
something really special for the
children of Warboys Primary
Academy.

💛

Pre‑Loved School Uniform

A quick reminder that our PTFA sell
high‑quality

pre‑loved uniform

through their Facebook page. It’s a
great way to save money, support the
school, and give uniform items a new
life.Please check out their page if you
need any extra bits for the term

HERE.
